newsitem.title: USA: Shoney's sues to block special meeting.
newsitem.headline: Shoney's sues to block special meeting.

text.p: Shoney's Inc said Thursday that it had begun litigation in Tennessee state court seeking to uphold bylaw amendments adopted by its board and to invalidate a dissident group's call for a special meeting.

The company amended its bylaws to clarify procedures for special meetings after a dissident group led by Raymond Schoenbaum, son of the Shoney's founder, called for a special meeting August 19 in a bid to replace the company's board.
Shoney's said in a statement Thursday that Tennessee law permits shareholders owning at least 10 percent of a company's stock to demand a special shareholder meeting.
Schoenbaum and his mother control eight percent of the company's stock.
"These amendments were adopted for the purpose of creating orderly procedures for the call and conduct of special meetings," Shoney's said in a statement.

"Mr. Schoenbaum's continued assertion that he can call a special shareholders' meeting at this time when he owns less than 10 percent of the company's stock is simple wrong, and our bylaw amendments are clearly valid," the company said.
